title: 1983 AHSME Problem 22
statement: Consider the two functions \[ \begin{aligned} f(x)&=x^2+2bx+1,\\ g(x)&=2a(x+b), \end{aligned} \] where the variable \(x\) and the constants \(a\) and \(b\) are real numbers. Each such pair of constants \(a\) and \(b\) may be considered as a point \((a,b)\) in an \(ab\)-plane. Let \(S\) be the set of such points \((a,b)\) for which the graphs of \(y=f(x)\) and \(y=g(x)\) do not intersect (in the \(xy\)-plane). The area of \(S\) is

solutions.text:
Intersections correspond to roots of \[ x^2+2(b-a)x+(1-2ab)=0. \] There are no real roots exactly when its discriminant is negative: \[ \begin{aligned} &4(b-a)^2-4(1-2ab)\\ &=4(a^2+b^2-1)\\ &\lt0. \end{aligned} \] Thus \(S\) is the interior of the unit circle in the \(ab\)-plane, with area \(\pi.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is B.
hints: Set \(f(x)=g(x)\) and require the resulting quadratic to have no real roots
Simplify the negative-discriminant condition in terms of \(a\) and \(b\)
